title: 1-byte write past the end of a 24-byte object into its neighbour
object: a, 24 bytes, the first of two consecutive st_alloc(24)
control: writes a[23] instead of a[24]; allocation traffic identical

asan.why: ASan checks shadow bytes; malloc objects are separated by redzones, arena objects are contiguous inside one poisoned-then-unpoisoned block unless the allocator re-poisons the gap

valgrind.why: Memcheck tracks addressability per malloc block; mempool requests restore per-object addressability

hwasan.why: tags are per 16-byte granule and per malloc; 24 rounds to 32 so a[24] is still in a's granule -- revisit the sizes (see C3.5)

ubsan.why: -fsanitize=bounds needs a statically known array bound; a pointer from an allocator has none

lowfat.why: bounds come from the malloc size class; an arena object inherits the whole arena's bounds
